comments.author: @Tamom318
comments.text:
Calling Sudan “Black Egypt” is deeply offensive and historically absurd. Sudan is NOT a black version of Egypt. We are Sudanese, with our own ancient identity and a proud Nubian heritage stretching back thousands of years. Our ancestors built Kerma and Kush, ruled from Napata and Meroë, raised pyramids along the Nile, and Kushite kings once ruled Egypt itself. Sudan does not need to be defined as somebody else’s version of Egypt. Our civilization stands proudly on its own.

And Sudan as a whole is NOT “Sahel.” The Sahel is a geographic belt that extends into western Sudan, especially Darfur. You cannot take Darfur’s regional geography and apply it to an enormous and incredibly diverse country.

Northern and much of central Sudan belong historically and culturally to the Nile Valley, with deep Nubian, Arab, Beja and other Sudanese influences. Linguistically, ethnically and culturally, these regions are not Sahelian. Darfur itself is diverse, but it has much stronger geographic, historical and cultural connections to the wider Sahel than northern and central Sudan do.

Sudan sits at the crossroads of the Nile Valley, Sahara, Sahel, Red Sea and the African interior. We are not “Black Egypt” and we are not simply another “Sahel country.” Sudan is Sudan. The land of Nubia, Kush and Meroë, with an identity and history of its own. We are not part of North Africa, east Africa or the Horn of Africa!! We have our own category Northeast Africa is where we stand. 🇸🇩
